This JSDoc comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon. Prefer two separate sentences over a semicolon.

Rewrite as two sentences, for example:

```ts
/** Identifies the list surface consuming the hook. Concurrent surfaces must use distinct scopes. */
```

This JSDoc comment uses an em dash to attach a trailing clause. Comments should be written as plain sentences without em dashes.

Rewrite without the em dash, for example:

```ts
/** Actions to render in the unified list. Oldest-first, because this view starts at the top and is not inverted. */
```

This JSDoc comment uses an em dash to append a qualifying clause. Comments should read as plain, natural sentences without stylistic tics like em dashes.

Rewrite without the em dash, for example:

```ts
/** The visible actions (FlatList `data` domain) that the marker scan runs over. Newest-first, or oldest-first when `isReversed`. */
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences. This one uses a semicolon to join two clauses instead of writing two separate sentences.

Split the sentence at the semicolon:

```diff
-            // The cards are rendered from the live action; the press is what runs into the deleted first match.
+            // The cards are rendered from the live action. The press is what runs into the deleted first match.
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences. This one uses a semicolon to join two clauses instead of writing two separate sentences.

Split the sentence at the semicolon:

```diff
-        // Wide layouts open the report first and the pressed expense on a short timer; let that timer run. Narrow layouts
+        // Wide layouts open the report first and the pressed expense on a short timer. Let that timer run. Narrow layouts
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences. This one joins two independent clauses with a semicolon instead of writing two separate sentences.

Split the sentence at the semicolon:

```diff
-                // rather than deleting it. An absent report is fine, the RHP loads it; a present one with no reportID is not.
+                // rather than deleting it. An absent report is fine, the RHP loads it. A present one with no reportID is not.
```

This comment uses an em dash (`...as the selection grows past 9 or 99 — a selection can cover far more rows...`).

Replace the em dash with a period, e.g. `...so the bar does not resize as the selection grows past 9 or 99. A selection can cover far more rows than are on screen.`

This header comment uses an em dash (`...to render a subtree inverted, which colors everything inside it — including popovers...`).

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g. `...which colors everything inside it, including popovers, which read the theme themselves and so cannot be inverted with style props.`

This prop comment uses an em dash (`Whether \`selectedCount\` is still being resolved — a "select all matching" selection...`).

Replace the em dash with a period, e.g. `Whether \`selectedCount\` is still being resolved. A "select all matching" selection only learns its real size once the server reports it.`

This comment uses an em dash (`...until it lands — otherwise a bar that turns out to be too wide...`).

Rewrite as two sentences, e.g. `...so it is kept hidden until it lands. Otherwise a bar that turns out to be too wide is briefly on screen at that width.`

This comment uses an em dash (`...whatever the container is doing — which makes these worth keeping.`).

Replace it with plain sentence punctuation, e.g. `...whatever the container is doing, which makes these worth keeping.`

This header comment uses an em dash (`render it as the last child of the view the table fills — pass a \`bottom\`...`).

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g. `...render it as the last child of the view the table fills. Pass a \`bottom\` through \`style\` to clear anything else pinned to that container...`

This comment uses an em dash (`How many that is comes from the bar's own fitting pass — see \`BulkActionBar\` below.`).

Replace the em dash with a period, e.g. `...comes from the bar's own fitting pass. See \`BulkActionBar\` below.`

This comment uses a semicolon to join two independent sentences (`...given a button of their own; the rest stay reachable behind "More".`).

Use two sentences, e.g. `...are given a button of their own. The rest stay reachable behind "More".`

This prop comment joins two clauses with a semicolon (`How many actions to give a button of their own; the rest go behind "More".`).

Split into two sentences, e.g. `How many actions to give a button of their own. The rest go behind "More". Decided by the fitting pass.`

This header comment uses an em dash (`which \`BulkActionBar\` inverts — so the surface...`).

Replace it with plain sentence punctuation, e.g. `...which \`BulkActionBar\` inverts, so the surface, the buttons and the "More" menu all read as one layer...`

This comment uses a semicolon to join two independent sentences (`...so it stands out against the table; its menus read as the popovers...`).

Use two sentences instead, e.g. `...so it stands out against the table. Its menus read as the popovers they are everywhere else in the app.`

This comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon (`...opens those items in a menu above itself; every other action runs \`onSelected\` directly.`).

Split it into two sentences, e.g. `...opens those items in a menu above itself. Every other action runs \`onSelected\` directly.`

This comment uses an em dash (`without a bounce — the default spring...`).

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g. `...so it arrives quickly and without a bounce. The default spring wobbles noticeably over this short a travel.`

Comments should read as plain sentences without em dashes. This line uses an em dash (`— keep it in step with \`bulkActionBar\``).

Replace the em dash with a period and start a new sentence, e.g. `...only used to reserve the space it floats over. Keep it in step with \`bulkActionBar\`.`

This comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon (`The rows are the scroller; the sub-header follows it through ...`). Per the plain-comment-style rule, use two separate sentences instead of a semicolon.

Suggested fix:

```ts
 * A group's sticky column sub-header and its transaction rows are separate FlashList rows, so they cannot share one
 * scroll container. The rows are the scroller. The sub-header follows it through `useHorizontalScrollFollower`, which
 * is what keeps the column labels lined up with the values below them once the table is wider than the viewport.
```

The comment uses a semicolon to join two independent clauses. Write it as two separate sentences instead.

```tsx
/** A workspace's avatar sized and colored for a list row. The subscript border follows the row's focus/hover state. */
```

The comment uses a semicolon to join two independent clauses. Write it as two separate sentences instead.

```tsx
/** A report's avatar(s) sized and colored for a list row. The subscript border follows the row's focus/hover state. */
```

The comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon. Comments should read as plain, natural sentences rather than semicolon-spliced clauses.

Split it into two sentences:
```tsx
/** Row footer naming the secondary login that added the member. Shared by the UserListItem family. The row gates rendering. */
```

This comment joins two independent sentences with a semicolon. Use a period between the two complete sentences instead.

```ts
// Already-consumed (nullish) entries are skipped. Clearing them again would just fire this callback once more.
```

The ESLint-disable justification uses a semicolon to splice two independent clauses (`...must fall back to the component report ID; ?? would retain the empty string.`). Comments should read as plain sentences, using a full stop rather than a semicolon to separate two complete thoughts.

Split it into two sentences:

```tsx
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/prefer-nullish-coalescing -- The existing || fallback is intentional. An empty policy-chat report ID must fall back to the component report ID, whereas ?? would retain the empty string.
```

Several newly added comments in this file use em dashes (`—`) and semicolons to join clauses, which the plain-comment-style rule disallows (this JSDoc block and the ones on `getConstInitializer` and `create` are all affected). Comments should read as plain sentences.

Replace em dashes with periods/commas and split semicolon-joined clauses into separate sentences, e.g.:
```js
 * Matches `variables.fontSizeNormal`, `variables.lineHeightXLarge`, and friends. This is the named escape
 * hatch around the typography scale. Only the `variables` module is matched. Unrelated objects that
 * happen to have a `fontSize*` key are left alone.
```

This newly added comment uses an em dash (`—`), which the plain-comment-style rule disallows.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:
```js
// `lineHeight*` steps above `pageHeader`). Adding those is a design call, not a refactor, so there
```

This comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon, which the plain-comment-style rule flags. Split it into two separate sentences so it reads like plain prose.

```tsx
{/* MenuItem.Root's built-in padding is ph5 (20px). mhn1 pulls it back to ph4 (16px) to align with the section title */}
```

This JSDoc line joins two separate instructions with a semicolon ("Pass `policies` from the picker and autocomplete; omit it for display/validation..."). Write them as two sentences:

```ts
 * ... Pass `policies` from the picker and autocomplete. Omit it for display/validation so already-selected values still resolve to labels.
```

This comment uses a semicolon to join two independent sentences, which the plain-comment-style rule flags. Split it into two sentences:

```ts
// Migrated Control workspaces leave areRulesEnabled undefined. Fall back to Classic category rules in that case.
```

This newly added comment uses em dashes to set off a parenthetical clause. Per the plain comment style guideline, comments should read as plain sentences without em/en dashes.

Rewrite it without the em dashes, for example:

```ts
// When the workspace has approval workflow rules, the rules name the first approver instead of the legacy employeeList.
```

This comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon. Comments should read as plain sentences, using two separate sentences instead of a semicolon.

Split it into two sentences:
```tsx
// The row itself is inert. Only the Switch handles the toggle so the menu stays open.
```

This comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon. Comments should read as plain sentences, using two separate sentences instead of a semicolon.

Split it into two sentences:
```tsx
// The row itself is inert. Only the Switch handles the toggle so the menu stays open.
```

This component comment uses an em dash (`—`), which CONSISTENCY-16 flags.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:
```tsx
/** Field preset: a field name plus its value. With no `value` the name takes over the row */
```

This prop comment uses two em dashes (`—`), which CONSISTENCY-16 flags.

Rewrite without the em dashes, e.g.:
```tsx
/** Value the field holds. Omit it, or pass an empty string, for a field not filled in yet */
```

This prop comment uses an em dash (`—`), which CONSISTENCY-16 flags.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:
```tsx
/** Typography layered on top of the shared base. Each leaf brings its own size and line height */
```

This prop comment uses an em dash (`—`), which CONSISTENCY-16 flags.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:
```tsx
/** Defaults to 2. Supporting text wraps, unlike primary text, which is always one line */
```

This prop comment uses an em dash (`—`), which CONSISTENCY-16 flags.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:
```tsx
/** Required here because the row builds its label from strings and can't read one out of an element */
```

This comment uses an em dash (`—`), which CONSISTENCY-16 flags. Comments should read as plain, natural sentences without stylistic tics like em dashes.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:
```tsx
/** Supporting text under a `MenuItem.Title`, the bottom line of a `MenuItem.Content` */
```

This comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon. Per the plain-comment-style guideline, comments should read like natural prose and use two separate sentences instead of a semicolon.

Split the sentence at the semicolon:

```ts
// The Search path has no separate report NVP source here. The archived flag and private_isArchived
// both derive from the same NVP, so the option's archived flag is the equivalent input.
privateIsArchived: !!isReportArchived,
```

The comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon (`The page does not read the navigation prop; this inert double...`). Prefer two separate sentences.

```ts
// The page does not read the navigation prop. This inert double only satisfies the navigator-provided prop.
```

The comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon (`The page does not read the navigation prop; this inert double...`). Prefer two separate sentences.

```ts
// The page does not read the navigation prop. This inert double only satisfies the navigator-provided prop.
```

The comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon (`...the pages branch on are set; \`createMock\` keeps the partial...`). Comments read more clearly as separate sentences.

Split into two sentences:
```ts
/**
 * A pending USD account. Only the handful of fields the pages branch on are set. `createMock` keeps the partial
 * type-checked against the real ACH shape, so renaming one of those fields fails the build instead of silently
 * leaving the fixture describing an object production no longer emits.
 */
```

This newly added comment uses an em dash ("anchored to one — including a"). Comments should be plain sentences without em dashes.

Example fix:
```tsx
{/* An expense carousel is shown wherever this report is anchored to one, including a
    one-transaction report opened straight from Home, which is not a search screen. The
    report-level carousel is search-only, since it pages through search results. */}
```

This newly added comment uses an em dash ("— and it inflates"). Comments should read as plain sentences without em dashes.

Split it into two sentences or use a comma:
```ts
 * the "0" placeholder rather than a real report, so paging onto it lands the user on an empty report. It also inflates
 * the "x of y" counter with a report the Reports list never showed them.
```

This comment uses an em dash (`replaces global fetch with expo/fetch — which needs ReadableStream`). Rewrite without the em dash.

Example:

```js
 * and, when falsy, replaces global fetch with expo/fetch. That needs ReadableStream (absent in
 * Hermes) and breaks every API request.
```

This header comment uses an em dash (`populate EXPO_PUBLIC_* values at runtime — which doesn't exist under Re.Pack`). Split into two sentences.

Example:

```js
 * populate EXPO_PUBLIC_* values at runtime. That integration doesn't exist under Re.Pack, leaving
 * them undefined.
```

This comment trails off with an em dash (`silently reuses stale transform output after a babel/loader/.env change —`). End the sentence with a period instead of a dangling em dash.

Example:

```js
// without this the cache silently reuses stale transform output after a babel, loader, or .env change.
```

This header comment uses an em dash (`register Fabric view configs — without it the app crashes on boot`). Split into two plain sentences.

Example:

```js
 * codegen plugin to register Fabric view configs. Without it the app crashes on boot.
```

This comment wraps a clause in a pair of em dashes (`we inline the whole initializer — interop call and literal require together — down to each use site`). Use commas or parentheses instead.

Example:

```js
 * to add the module to the graph at all. So instead of hoisting the helper, we inline the whole
 * initializer (the interop call and the literal require together) down to each use site.
```

This comment uses an em dash (`stay hoisted and eager — about half of all imports here`). Rewrite without the em dash.

Example:

```js
 * default and namespace imports stay hoisted and eager. That is about half of all imports here,
 * and exactly the cycle tolerance the loader exists to provide.
```

This comment uses an em dash (`emits a memoizing wrapper function per imported module — ~103k extra functions here`). Replace the em dash with a plain sentence break.

Example:

```js
 * imports, but SWC's lazy mode emits a memoizing wrapper function per imported module. That is
 * about 103k extra functions here, worth about 7MB of Hermes bytecode.
```

This header comment uses an em dash (`defers each \`require()\` to its first use site — the same import-cycle tolerance...`). Comments should read as plain sentences without em dashes.

Rewrite as two sentences:

```js
 * Lowers ES modules to CommonJS and defers each `require()` to its first use site. This gives the
 * same import-cycle tolerance Metro gets from `inlineRequires` (see metro.config.js), which this
 * app relies on to boot.
```

This comment uses a semicolon to join two independent statements (`does real DCE + tree-shake; commander last-wins`) and a redundant parenthetical (`(Metro-era assumption)`), which read like stylistic tics rather than plain prose.

Split into two plain sentences, e.g.:

```groovy
// Force `--minify true` for Repack. The RN gradle task hardcodes minifyEnabled=false when Hermes is on, an assumption from the Metro era.
// Under Repack the SWC minifier does real dead-code elimination and tree-shaking, and commander applies the last value wins.
extraPackagerArgs = ["--minify", "true"]
```

This JSDoc line uses a semicolon to join two independent clauses ("...so the exclusion holds regardless of which bucket the back end assigns the violation to; names in `excludedNoticeNames` are dropped from the notice check only."). Per the plain-comment-style guideline, use two separate sentences instead of a semicolon.

Rewrite as two sentences:

```ts
 * bucket the back end assigns the violation to. Names in `excludedNoticeNames` are dropped from the notice check only.
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences. This comment uses a semicolon to join two independent clauses instead of writing two separate sentences, which the plain-comment-style guideline flags.

Split the two clauses into separate sentences:

```ts
// A submitted `companyCardRequired` is not actionable by the submitter, so it must not drive the RBR. It is excluded by name because the back end owns its type.
```

This newly added comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon, which the plain-comment-style guideline calls out. Comments should read as separate, natural sentences rather than splicing two statements together with a semicolon.

Split it into two sentences:

```tsx
// Reports cannot know the exact all-matching count until the final page is loaded. Until then this is
// the selected loaded-report count. It becomes authoritative as soon as the final page is loaded.
count: areAllMatchingItemsSelected ? selectedAllMatchingItemsCount : selectedItemsCount,
```

This newly added comment uses a semicolon to splice two independent clauses into one line, which CONSISTENCY-16 flags. Comments should read as plain sentences and split independent thoughts into separate sentences rather than joining them with a semicolon.

Split it into two sentences, for example:

```ts
// delegateAccountID will be threaded in PR 16 together with the other openReport params.
// buildOptimisticAddCommentReportAction falls back to the module-level Onyx.connect value (https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/66425)
delegateAccountID: undefined,
```

This JSDoc line uses en dashes (`–`) to set off a clause: `...has any card feed – an Expensify Card feed OR a company card feed – which makes...`. Comments should read like plain, natural sentences without em/en dashes.

Rewrite without the dashes, for example:

```ts
/**
 * Returns whether the domain has any card feed, either an Expensify Card feed or a company card feed, which makes
 * the domain-group "Card preferred workspace" setting eligible to be enabled. Reads the domain-scoped keys so
 * eligibility stays scoped to feeds owned by this domain and avoids cross-domain false positives.
 */
```

This comment joins two independent statements with a semicolon (`Reset when the external value is cleared; ignore other external changes while editing.`). Comments should read as plain sentences, so use two separate sentences instead of a semicolon.

```ts
// Reset when the external value is cleared. Ignore other external changes while editing.
```

The added JSDoc sentence uses an em dash (`trust — "not loaded yet"`), which the plain-comment style guideline disallows. Comments should read as plain sentences without em/en dashes.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:
```ts
 * This never returns `undefined`: an unloaded NVP answers `true`, so `false` is the only value a caller can
 * trust, because "not loaded yet" and "onboarded" are indistinguishable.
```

This newly added comment uses an em dash in its own sentence, which the plain-comment-style guideline asks us to avoid. Write it as two plain sentences (or join with a conjunction) instead.

```ts
// Then nothing is sent. An unfiltered grouped query would return every card the user has
```

This newly added JSDoc comment uses an em dash in its own prose, which the plain-comment style guideline avoids.

Rewrite the sentence without the em dash, for example:
```ts
    /**
     * Whether this rule belongs to the policy's default workflow, the one shown as approving for "Everyone".
     *
     * ...
     */
```

This newly added comment uses an em dash in its own prose, which the plain-comment style guideline avoids.

Rewrite without the em dash, for example:
```ts
 * Without this they end up covered by no rule at all and resolve through the legacy `employeeList.submitsTo`,
 * which still names whoever approved for them before the default workflow was last edited, so they render as a
 * workflow of their own around a stale approver.
```

This newly added comment uses an em dash in its own prose, which the plain-comment style guideline avoids.

Replace the em dash with plain phrasing, for example:
```ts
 * "already in a workflow" for the purpose of warning about cross-workflow moves. Only members routed to some
 * other approver are.
```

This newly added comment uses em dashes, which the plain-comment style guideline avoids in a comment's own prose.

Rewrite the sentence without em dashes, for example:
```ts
 * The marker is only written when the default workflow is saved through the rules backend, so policies that
 * predate it, or have never had their default workflow edited, have none. Callers use this to decide
```

This newly added JSDoc joins two independent clauses with a semicolon. Per the plain-comment-style guidance, prefer two separate sentences over a semicolon so the comment reads like natural prose.

Split the clause into two sentences:

```ts
/**
 * Returns a transaction's amount with the sign it is displayed with. A transaction on an expense report, on a group
 * policy, unreported, or deleted keeps its sign. Any other transaction returns its magnitude.
 */
```

This JSDoc comment uses an em dash, which the plain-comment-style rule flags.

Replace the em dash with a sentence break, e.g.:
```ts
/**
 * The Submit intent runs on a free `submit` workspace, so unlike the other intents there is no free trial and
 * NVP_FIRST_DAY_FREE_TRIAL is unset. The 60-day window is anchored on NVP_PRIVATE_FIRST_POLICY_CREATED_DATE instead.
 */
```

This JSDoc line uses a semicolon to join two independent statements; the plain-comment-style rule asks for two separate sentences instead.

Split into two sentences, e.g.:
```ts
/**
 * Checks if the current date is within 60 days of the onboarding start date. Paid plans pass their trial start date.
 * Free plans (e.g. Submit) never start a trial, so they pass their first workspace creation date instead.
 * Returns false if no start date is provided.
 */
```

This newly added comment uses an em dash (`—`) in its own sentence (`...no longer edited from this flow — it lives on the Advanced page...`). Comments should read as plain, natural sentences without em dashes.

Replace the em dash with a separate sentence:

```ts
// The Default vendor row is now always visible on the company card page for whichever export destination is active, so subscribe to the matching vendor key unconditionally. `autoCreateVendor` is no longer edited from this flow. It lives on the Advanced page and is subscribed there.
```

This comment uses a semicolon to join two independent clauses instead of writing them as two separate sentences, which makes it read less like natural prose.

Split it into two sentences:

```ts
// Return a minimal IOU report for the money request report key so isExpenseReport is false and the early return is skipped. Everything else returns undefined.
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences without an em dash. This JSDoc line uses an em dash to join two clauses.

Replace the em dash with two separate sentences:
```ts
 * mounting for the same policy don't each fire a redundant `OpenPolicyTagsPage`
 * read. `API.read` does not dedupe in-flight reads, so we guard here instead.
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences without an em dash. This JSDoc line uses an em dash to join two clauses.

Replace the em dash with two separate sentences:
```ts
 * mounting for the same policy don't each fire a redundant `GetPolicyCategories`
 * read. `API.read` does not dedupe in-flight reads, so we guard here instead.
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences. This comment uses a semicolon to join two independent sentences; the style guide asks you to write them as two separate sentences.

Split into two sentences:

```ts
// The claim writeWhenReady settles once its write reaches (or fails to reach) the queue. The real
// gate is covered in SequentialQueueReadGateTest.
claimReadGateForDeferredWrite: jest.fn(() => ({handOff: jest.fn(), release: jest.fn()})),
```

This comment uses a semicolon to join two clauses (`Show the matching-report total once it lands; before then (or offline) fall back...`) instead of two separate sentences. Per the plain-comment-style guideline, prefer plain sentences over semicolon-joined clauses.

Rewrite as two sentences, for example:

```tsx
// Show the matching-report total once it lands. Before then, or while offline, fall back to the loaded-page report count.
```

The JSDoc uses the arrow notation `API <-> Middleware` instead of describing the relationship in plain words. Per the plain-comment-style rule, prefer natural prose over arrows in comments.

Rewrite it in words, for example:

```ts
 * Guards the wiring the fix for the import cycle between libs/API and Middleware depends on: loading the
 * app's composition root must attach the API middlewares.
```

This newly added JSDoc description uses em dashes (`—`) to join clauses, which the plain-comment style guideline flags. Comments should read as plain sentences without em/en dashes.

Rewrite the two em-dash sentences as ordinary sentences, e.g.:

```ts
 * report total. Each source transaction already stores `convertedAmount`, its amount in the *source report's*
 * currency, so as long as the copy lands in that same currency we can express every expense in the copy's currency
```

This comment joins two independent clauses with a semicolon. Per the plain-comment-style guideline, write two separate sentences instead.

Rewrite as separate sentences, e.g.:

```ts
// A header is only rendered in the table layout. Narrow layouts render rows as cards with no columns to size.
```

This comment uses an em dash, which the plain-comment-style guideline disallows. Comments should read as plain, natural sentences.

Rewrite without the em dash, e.g.:

```ts
 * Sizes the Search table's free-text columns from their content, instead of every one taking an equal share of what the
 * fixed columns leave over. Today that leaves a column of empty descriptions holding the same room as one of long
 * merchant names.
```

This newly added JSDoc uses an em dash (`—`) in its own prose, which makes the comment read less like something a person wrote. Comments should use plain sentences without em dashes.

Split the clause into two sentences (and drop the em dash), for example:

```ts
 * When the policy locks the reimbursable field (`disabledFields.reimbursable === true`, i.e. one of the two
 * "Always …" cash-expense modes), the split must follow the policy's `defaultReimbursable` regardless of the
 * parent expense's stored value. A pre-rule expense can still carry `reimbursable: true` under an
 * "Always non-reimbursable" workspace. Seeding the locked default also equals the value the
 * `shouldShowReimbursable` gate compares against, so the toggle hides automatically.
```

This added JSDoc uses an em dash ("A closing modal blurs focus so it can't be left on content that is about to unmount — but by then..."). Comments should avoid em dashes and read as plain sentences.

Suggested fix (split into two sentences):

```ts
* about to unmount. By then its focus trap may have already returned focus to the launcher that opened it, and
```

This added JSDoc uses an em dash ("The element that opened this modal — a popover's anchor"). Comments should avoid em dashes.

Replace the em dash with a comma:

```ts
* The element that opened this modal, a popover's anchor. Used only when nothing held focus at activation time,
```

This added JSDoc uses an em dash ("The element that opened this trap — a popover's anchor"). Comments should read as plain sentences without em dashes.

Replace the em dash with a comma or split into two sentences, e.g.:

```ts
* The element that opened this trap, a popover's anchor. Only consulted when `document.activeElement`
```

The comment uses an em dash. Rewrite it as a plain sentence.

```tsx
{/* Reset only makes sense while a condition is set, and only on a rule that isn't already saved
    against a category. An existing category rule is identified by its category. */}
```
The JSDoc for `clearPolicyCategoryTaxErrors` uses an em dash. Rewrite as a plain sentence, e.g. `... since there is no stored rule left to show. This matches how a failed coding rule is cleared.`

The JSDoc for `deletePolicyCategoryTaxes` uses an em dash. Rewrite as a plain sentence, e.g. `Shares one optimistic array across the writes for the same reason \`setPolicyCategoryTaxes\` does, so the whole selection is marked for deletion together...`

The JSDoc for `setPolicyCategoryTaxes` uses an em dash. Rewrite it as plain sentences, e.g. replace `— the last would simply overwrite the rest.` with `and the last would simply overwrite the rest.` on the preceding line.

The comment uses an em dash. Rewrite it as a plain sentence.

```tsx
// Sections stay grouped and in a fixed order whatever the column sort is. Sorting only reorders rows inside a section.
```

The comment uses an em dash, which the plain-comment-style rule asks us to avoid. Rewrite it as a plain sentence.

```tsx
// A single section stays a flat list. The headers only earn their place once there is more than one group to tell apart.
```

Comments should read as plain, natural sentences. This line joins two independent clauses with a semicolon (`...mistaken for a dead \`Button\`; state-shaped ones stay silent.`) instead of writing them as two separate sentences.
